So in my never-ending side quest which I call combinatorial game theory I've found the need to talk about the profinite integers - specifically, I need the fact that the absolute Galois group of a finite field is Z-hat. How should we go about defining these in Mathlib? I know that there is a definition within FLT of Zhat as a set of integer sequences, but I've also been told that this is likely not the correct/Mathlib approach.

Do we want to define ZHat as a direct limit? Do we want to define it as a special case of a more general profinite completion operator? What kind of API should we expose for it?
cc. @Aaron Liu @Kevin Buzzard
Can you define it as the product of the p-adic integers over all p?
I could, but there's like three other ways I could also define it
The question is not so much "can I do this" but rather "what's the best way I can do this"

My own idea is that the most elegant approach would be to first define the ProfiniteCompletion of a group (as the direct limit of the finite subquotients), and then define abbrev ZHat := ProfiniteCompletion ℤ
(But I'm also very unfamiliar with the theory, so I defer to others' expertise)
we have docs#ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion.completion
but it's only in this category theory language and it's only for multiplicative groups
what's up with that? sometimes it feels like the category theory library is some second codebase orthogonal to Mathlib
Can we make use of this categorical definition, or will we have to do things from scratch?
it's definitely usable
oh ok I'm glad to hear
you just need to unbundle everything

Aaron Liu said:

but it's only in this category theory language and it's only for multiplicative groups

I guess everything in that file can just be tagged with to_additive?
Do we want docs#Profinite in the root namespace to be the category, rather than some typeclass on groups?
profiniteness isn't just for groups
and you can also just spell it as [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]
Sorry, you can tell that I'm completely unfamiliar with category theory Mathlib

Violeta Hernández said:

what's up with that? sometimes it feels like the category theory library is some second codebase orthogonal to Mathlib

What's wrong with just using the category theory library? Category theory is an amazing language for doing mathematics
Mostly I'm worried about code duplication
Is it ok to have a file which defines the profinite completion of a group as some object in a category
but then also have a file which defines the profinite completion of a group as a type satisfying certain typeclasses?
should we use category theory to define the unbundled version, or use the unbundled version to define the category theory version?
do we have pre-existing examples of similar design?
Category theory is awesome I agree, I'm just confused about how it fits into the rest of the library

In general, it usually goes unbundled -> category theory. But in my opinion, when a definition is most conveniently phrased in categorical language (like stuff involving limits, such as profinite completion), then there is nothing wrong with going the other way (and maybe realize you don't even need the unbundled version, and just work with the object in the category)
You're right, I guess the profinite completion is a very categorical construction
So we have the profinite completion, we have the morphism into the profinite completion and the fact that it is dense
How would we build the morphisms Z^→Z/nZ\widehat{\mathbb Z}\to\mathbb Z/n\mathbb ZZ→Z/nZ? What's their generalization to the profinite completion setting?
apply docs#ProfiniteGrp.ProfiniteCompletion.lift to the quotient map from Z\mathbb{Z}Z to the finite (hence profinite) groups Z/nZ\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}Z/nZ
Oh yeah I guess finite groups are in fact profinite yeah
Final question before I get to work, what would be a good file for this? Does GroupTheory.Profinite work?
Actually I do have another question: when we use to_additive, do we want AddProfinite groups or MulProfinite groups?
(i.e. which do we treat as the default for Profinite?)

One thing I would suggest is to consider what the right abstraction would be if you would like to start developing profinite completion of more general algebraic structures. Presumably there is some abstract nonsense that can apply to categories of algebras over any finitary Lawvere theory. The cases of groups and rings are probably the most common in the literature, so treating those as special cases is of course still valuable.

I'm only really interested in the group structure of the profinite integers, since I need it for some results in CGT. But I'd imagine that the "correct" thing to do for Mathlib is to define it as the profinite completion of the ring of integers. That then gives us the universal property for free (modulo universes).
There are two universal properties, one for groups and one for rings, and you surely won't get both for free.

Intuitively I'd say that the profinite completions of ℤ as a group and as a ring are isomorphic, because they're the limits of the same diagrams. Maybe there's a category theoretic way to state this, something something forgetful functor.
Sure they're isomorphic, but AddSubgroup Int and Ideal Int aren't equal types.
It should be possible to say that the diagrams are isomorphic? Or something like that.
Sure
The type of normal additive subgroups of finite index of ℤ and the type of ideals defining finite quotients are isomorphic
what a mouthful

It seems much easier than to try to prove the universal property from scratch, knowing only the construction of ZHat as a subring of Π n : ℕ+, ZMod n

Introducing category theory at all makes some things easier and some things harder in practice. Going from a ring to an object in the category of rings and then back to a ring doesn't round-trip syntactically and this can create issues with type class inference.

Speaking of category theory, I need some help. I'm trying to define the canonical projection maps completion G →*ₜ G ⧸ H for H of finite index. My current code looks like this:

    completion G ⟶ ofFiniteGrp <| .of (G ⧸ H.toSubgroup) :=
  lift (GrpCat.ofHom <| QuotientGroup.mk' H.toSubgroup)

    eta G ≫ (forget₂ _ _).map (proj G H) = (GrpCat.ofHom <| QuotientGroup.mk' H.toSubgroup) :=
  lift_eta ..

    pi fun H : FiniteIndexNormalSubgroup G ↦ ofFiniteGrp <| .of (G ⧸ H.toSubgroup) :=
  lift (GrpCat.ofHom <| MonoidHom.pi fun H ↦ QuotientGroup.mk' H.toSubgroup)

@[to_additive]

First of all, the existence of docs#ProfiniteGrp.pi seems a bit weird to me. Do we not have a more general mechanism to talk about products within categories? And if we do, is there a more direct way to define piProj in terms of proj?

Second and more important... How do we actually prove that piProj is injective? I believe this would follow from knowing that, given x y : completion G, there's some open normal subgroup which contains one but not the other. If this is a lemma in the library somewhere I don't know how to find it.
And also... can we show Mono in ProfiniteGrp is equivalent to being injective? We have this result for GrpCat so I would imagine there's a one-line incantation for this.
Nevermind, I changed my approach and I think I figured out something nice.
If you’re still looking for mono iff injective, you can find it here: https://github.com/FormalFrontier/profinite-groups/blob/main/ProfiniteGroups/EpiMono.lean
I'd appreciate feedback on #44652. I'm entirely unfamiliar with how category theory works in Mathlib and I can't shake the feeling that I'm doing something wrong.

@Violeta Hernández took a very quick look, sorry that I don't have time for a full review. At first glance, my impression is that things like proj aren't really needed, as that is essentially already data in the limit cone that's used to define the profinite completion.

What's the proper way to write this map, then? x.val feels quite weird to me, since it's unfolding the definition of the completion. (Isn't the idea that we should be reasoning in terms of universal properties?)
Or is the idea that limitProj should stay while proj doesn't?

The entire universal property is bundled in limitConeIsLimit already. limitCone has a π field that bundles a natural transformation encoding the projections (didn’t try on an editor, but proj _ should be (limitCone F).π.app _).
If we want to get ride of the .val and only ever work with this through the language of category theory and to forget the concrete model for this limit, then limit F should be an abbrev for (limitCone F).pt, and then the IsLimit structure has all that we need.
(and then in this case limitCone shouldn’t be an abbrev but some no-exposed def if we really want to go down the "all of this is implementation detail" road)
On a related design note. I find it really weird that docs#ProfiniteGrp.limit is an abbrev for the not very well named docs#ProfiniteGrp.limitConePtAux.
If we are to keep it public (which I think there's good reason to), perhaps we could rename it to something like ProfiniteGrp.limitSubgroup?
